svg.title: The universal restricted spectral idempotent
svg.desc: A full compact coend defines the continuous transpose. Its module projection formula and actual diagonal coevaluation triangle give an invertible non-unital multiplication. Integrating enhanced Hecke eigen-families by continuous global sections gives the actual geometric idempotent. Closed support, open localization and a quadratic tensor kernel distinguish the claims and their scope.
svg.text: The actual diagonal triangle gives a geometric idempotent
Complex curves; every genus and bundle component; full unbounded Hecke action.
1. The continuous transpose uses the whole compact DG category — UID.1–UID.4
K = (id ⊗ L)(Rᵣ); (L ⊗ id)(K) = the actual coevaluation kernel in A ⊗ A.
D(a) = coend over T: Γ!(L(T∨) ⊗ a) ⊗ T.
Hom(S,D(a)) = Γ!(L(S∨) ⊗ a), for every compact S.
r ⊗ D(a) ≃ D(L(r) ⊗ a) for every r: compact dual tests, then full continuous bars.
All homogeneous maps and higher action coherences remain in these coends.
2. The full triangle gives multiplication and its explicit inverse — UID.5–UID.11
L D(a) = (id ⊗ Γ!)(K(coev) ⊗ (1 ⊠ a)) ≃ a.
p ⊗ p → D L(p) → p: both arrows are equivalences.
The inverse reverses these arrows; the coend maps are the actual algebra product.
The multiplication is commutative and non-unital; no map 1 → p is assumed.
3. Enhanced families give the actual geometric endofunctor — UID.12–UID.15
Hᵣ(M) = K-action modules in M ⊗ A; free induction F(K) is left adjoint to U(K).
P(enh)(m) = F(K)(m ⊠ 1): the two Ran actions give the full Hecke eigen-isomorphisms.
Πᵣ(m) = (id ⊗ Γ!) U(K) P(enh)(m) = Φ(p)m.
Equivalently: coend Γ!(L(T∨)) ⊗ Φ(T)m; hence Πᵣ Πᵣ ≃ Πᵣ.
On BunG, Φ is the actual geometric transfer-kernel action, in all module degrees.
4. Three tests separate idempotence from its image — UID.16–UID.20
Closed t-support: p(t) = fib(C[t] → C[t,t⁻¹]); H¹ = t⁻¹C[t⁻¹].
H⁰(p(t)) = 0: a nonzero supported p(t) cannot have an algebra unit.
Open t-localization: p(u) = C[t,t⁻¹], with its ordinary unit; the two images differ.
For C[t][z,z⁻¹], |z| = −2: closed H¹⁻²ʳ is principal parts, open H⁻²ʳ is Laurent.
For principal parts P: P ⊗ over B with P = 0, but Tor₁(P,P) = P; the derived square survives.
5. Ordinary sections give a different, non-idempotent object — UID.21–UID.24
Replacing Γ! on compact coefficients gives q = C[[t]].
q ⊗ over C[t] with q → q has a nonzero kernel.
Let f² = 1+t, f(0)=1; F=C(t), K=C((t)), E=F(f) is quadratic.
E ⊗ over F with K = K × K; f ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ f maps to (0,−2f) ≠ 0.
This element survives in K ⊗ over F with K but multiplication kills it.
Every finite t-adic jet kills the difference: finite jets do not detect the full kernel.
Exact proofs: §§3.186–3.193, UID.1–UID.24; Solutions3.DG–3.DI.
Nilpotent singular-support image and original-field regularity need their further proofs.
Universal-projector framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2.
